summary: Do not ship yet. S-1 is resolved: the original blue/zinc ramps are restored, named dark tokens isolate the redesigned palette, the dark semantic mapping uses them, and N34 pins absolute light/dark values. However, the fix introduces a high-risk split accent contract that N34 does not detect.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: Raw-blue public primitives bypass the new dark palette seam
findings.body: The shared accent contract still exposes `bg-blue-600`, and the shared focus contract similarly uses `blue-500`. Restoring those base ramps changes dark switches, selected chips, and legacy focus rings back to #0066cc/#0071e3, while semantic Button/Checkbox consumers use the redesigned #1d4ed8/#2563eb. Ticket 05 and later settings work would copy this split interface, making independent theme changes require cross-component surgery. N34 only probes root semantic properties, so it passes while rendered primitives diverge. This is distinct from the explicitly deferred raw-zinc gap.
findings.recommendation: Move shared accent and focus fragments—and direct checked/pressed consumers such as ToggleSwitch and ChipGroup—to `primary`/`ring` semantic utilities. Extend the smoke assertion to inspect representative rendered checked, selected, and focused controls in both themes.

next_steps: Unify raw-blue active and focus consumers behind the semantic palette seam.
Run N34 and the full smoke suite after adding rendered-control assertions.
